claim: applyLadderToPreset decides what mode a Favorite names (`named`) by sanitising the preset. Favorites never store Clear HDR: neither the server payload (`buildCurrentPresetPayload`) nor the touch UI's `cameraPresetSettings` writes it. `presetSettings` starts from `camera_.settings()` (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10927), so `named` takes Clear HDR from whatever the camera runs now. When the camera's current resolution and the Favorite's resolution differ in Clear HDR, the identity is wrong, sameMode fails, and apply_preset is refused even though the ladder would load exactly what the Favorite recorded.
scenario: Ladder is [3840x2160:16:hdr:none:25, 3840x2160:12:sdr:none] on an IMX585 in cDNG. The camera is on Resolution 1 (Clear HDR on). The user loads a Favorite saved on Resolution 2 (cameraResolution 3840x2160, cameraRawBitDepth 12, cameraFps 50). presetSettings.clearHdr stays true, so sanitize gives named = 4K Clear HDR 12-bit. The ladder picks Resolution 2 (4K SDR 12-bit). The reply is ok:false: "This Favorite records 4K Clear HDR 12-bit at 50 fps; the Mode Ladder runs 50 fps in 4K SDR 12-bit...". The reverse also fails. On Resolution 2, a Resolution-1 Favorite (16-bit, 24 fps) gets supportedRawBitDepthForSensor(Imx585, 16, clearHdr=false) = 12, so named = 4K SDR 12-bit against the ladder's 4K Clear HDR 16-bit, and it is refused. A 2K binned Favorite loaded while on a Clear HDR resolution is sanitised to 4K Clear HDR 12-bit and refused too. Saving the Favorite again cannot fix any of these, because Clear HDR is never stored.
fix: Do not take Clear HDR from the camera when deciding what the Favorite names. In applyLadderToPreset, use `CaptureSettings asNamed = preset; asNamed.clearHdr = chosen.clearHdr; const ladder::Rung named = ladderRungOf(sanitizeSettingsForSensor(asNamed, sensorFamily));`. Also refuse when that sanitise changed the Favorite's own size or bits: compare named.width/height/bits with `normalizedResolutionForSensor(sensorFamily, preset.resolution)` (with the 3840x2200→3840x2160 Core alias) and preset.rawBitDepth. Without that check, a 2K-binned SDR Favorite would be silently forced to 4K when the ladder picks a Clear HDR resolution, which is the reviewer's suggested fix taken alone. For the message, label the Favorite by its stored size and bits, under the Clear HDR value that keeps them (SDR when both do).
evidence: I traced the code and the claim holds. A Favorite has no Clear HDR field. buildCurrentPresetPayload (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:6719-6810) writes cameraResolution/Width/Height, cameraRawBitDepth and cameraFps but no clear_hdr. The touch UI's ApertarControlBridge::cameraPresetSettings (ui/src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1152-1183) does the same. apply_preset starts from `CaptureSettings presetSettings = camera_.settings();` (App:10927) and never reads a Clear HDR key: grep finds no clearHdr in the handler. So presetSettings.clearHdr is whatever the camera runs now. applyLadderToPreset (CameraController.cpp:10733-10751) computes `named = ladderRungOf(sanitizeSettingsForSensor(preset, sensorFamily))`. sanitize uses clearHdr in two places: `supportedRawBitDepthForSensor(..., settings.clearHdr)` (2893), where IMX585 SDR turns 16 into 12 (2855-2858), and `if (Imx585 && clearHdr) resolution = 3840x2160` (2897-2898). sameMode (ModeLadder.hpp:88-91) compares clearHdr. Scenario 1: the camera is on 4K Clear HDR 16 and the Favorite is 3840x2160/12/50. named is 4K Clear HDR 12. ladderRewriteLocked → chooseRung(50) skips rung 1 (ceiling 25, ModeLadder.hpp:155) and picks rung 2 (IMX585 4K SDR, 60 or 30 per table 2813). So runs is 4K SDR 12, sameMode is false, and the call is refused with the false text "This Favorite records 4K Clear HDR 12-bit at 50 fps". Scenario 2 (reverse): on SDR, a 16-bit/24 fps Favorite sanitises to SDR 12, while chooseRung(24) picks rung 1 (Clear HDR 16). Refused again, although the ladder would load exactly what was saved. namesMode is true for both writers, because cameraRawBitDepth and cameraResolution are always present (App:11178-11180). This breaks SPEC.md:142, which says to refuse only when the preset names a mode the ladder would not run and otherwise to rewrite. Whether a Favorite loads depends on the camera's current resolution, not on the Favorite. Saving again does not help, because Clear HDR is still not stored.

claim: In Standby, setBuildMaximumFps stores the new maximum and returns at `state_ != CameraState::Ready` without the ladder rewrite (SPEC 2.4 lists setBuildMaximumFps as a rewrite point). wakeFromStandby (9216-9229) only restarts the session, which caps the FPS. It has no ladder guard like start() and does not persist. After waking, the camera runs a resolution the ladder would not choose for the new FPS.
scenario: The camera is on Resolution 2 (4K SDR 12-bit, up to 50) at 50 fps and in standby. Config is saved with [camera] max_fps=24. On wake, session_->start caps the FPS to 24 in 4K SDR 12-bit. ladder_rung stays 2 (its ceiling is now 24), although chooseRung(24) picks Resolution 1 (4K Clear HDR 16-bit). The next take records SDR 12-bit at 24 fps until some later set_fps moves the camera. The capped 24 fps is also never written to camera_settings.conf.
fix: In wakeFromStandby, after `settings_ = session_->currentSettings(); state_ = CameraState::Ready;`, add the same guard as start(). That is: `CaptureSettings onLadder = settings_; const bool ladderMoves = ladderRewriteLocked(onLadder); if (ladderMoves || std::abs(onLadder.fps - settings_.fps) > 0.0001) applyFpsStepLocked(onLadder.fps, false, true, ladderMoves ? &onLadder : nullptr);`, then `persistSettingsLocked();` before emitSettingsEventLocked(). This also covers a mode_ladder or settings change made while in standby.
evidence: I traced the code and the gap is real. setBuildMaximumFps (CameraController.cpp:10162-10179) stores the maximum and then returns at `if (state_ != CameraState::Ready || recording_) return;` (10168) before the T34 `ladderRewriteLocked(next)` at 10172. The function can run in Standby: POST /api/config (App:7380-7390) calls `camera_.setBuildMaximumFps(cameraMaxFpsFromHardwareConfig())` whatever the camera state is. wakeFromStandby (9216-9232) only runs `session_->start(settings_)`, whose sanitise caps the FPS through buildMaximumFps (6427; maximumSupportedFpsForResolution 2830-2837), and then `settings_ = session_->currentSettings()`. It has no ladderRewriteLocked guard, unlike start() at 9154-9162, and it does not call persistSettingsLocked. Scenario: ladder [4K ClearHDR16 up to 25, 4K SDR12]. The camera is on SDR12 at 50 or 30 fps, goes into standby, and max_fps=24 is saved. On wake it runs 4K SDR 12 at 24, and findRung still reports rung 2. But chooseRung(24) returns rung 1, the first with ceiling >= 24 (ModeLadder.hpp:155), whose ceiling is min(25, 24). In Ready state the same config save would move to Clear HDR 16 (10172-10175). SPEC.md §2.4 lists setBuildMaximumFps as a rewrite point, and the ladder's rule (FPS picks the resolution outside a take) is broken until the next set_fps. Severity is low. The missing persist is partly older behaviour (T33's wake did not persist either).

claim: applyLadderToPreset works out the mode a Favorite names with `sanitizeSettingsForSensor(preset)`. Favorites never store Clear HDR: apply_preset sets no clearHdr field, and neither the touch UI's cameraPresetSettings nor the WebUI's allowedKeys sends one. So `preset.clearHdr` is whatever the camera runs right now. Whether a Favorite is refused therefore depends on the resolution the camera happens to be on, not on what the Favorite names.
scenario: IMX585, ladder Resolution 1 = 4K Clear HDR 16-bit up to 25, Resolution 2 = 4K SDR 12-bit up to 50. (a) Save a Favorite on Resolution 1: cameraResolution 3840x2160, cameraRawBitDepth 16, cameraFps 24. Move to 48 fps (Resolution 2, clearHdr=false) and load the Favorite. The 16-bit SDR settings are sanitised to 12 bits, so named = 4K SDR 12-bit. The ladder at 24 runs 4K Clear HDR 16-bit. Result: refused with "This Favorite records 4K SDR 12-bit at 24 fps; the Mode Ladder runs 24 fps in 4K Clear HDR 16-bit...", even though that is exactly the mode the Favorite was saved in. (b) The other way round: a Favorite saved on Resolution 2 (12-bit, 48 fps) and loaded while on Resolution 1 gives named = 4K Clear HDR 12-bit and is refused against 4K SDR 12-bit. "Save the Favorite again" does not help, because the problem returns from the other class.
fix: In applyLadderToPreset, work out `named` from a copy whose Clear HDR follows the ladder's choice. On IMX585, 16-bit exists only as Clear HDR, so a 16-bit Favorite must not read as SDR 12-bit: `CaptureSettings namedSettings = preset; namedSettings.clearHdr = chosen.clearHdr || preset.rawBitDepth == 16; const ladder::Rung named = ladderRungOf(sanitizeSettingsForSensor(namedSettings, sensorFamily));`
evidence: ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10915 `CaptureSettings presetSettings = camera_.settings();`. The handler (10888-11186) never sets clearHdr. The touch UI's cameraPresetSettings (ui/src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1152-1185) has no Clear HDR key, and neither does the WebUI allowedKeys list (WebControlPage.cpp:12160-12239). CameraController.cpp:10742 `const ladder::Rung named = ladderRungOf(sanitizeSettingsForSensor(preset, sensorFamily));` therefore uses the live clearHdr. supportedRawBitDepthForSensor (2840-2864) maps IMX585 16-bit with clearHdr=false to 12. sameMode (ModeLadder.hpp:88-91) compares clearHdr. Scenario (a): live on Resolution 2 (SDR), Favorite has 16-bit, 3840x2160, 24 fps. named = 4K SDR 12-bit. chooseRung(24) gives Resolution 1, so runs = 4K Clear HDR 16-bit. The mismatch reaches setErrorLocked at 10745, so the Favorite is refused even though the ladder runs the mode it was saved in. Scenario (b) holds the same way, with named = 4K Clear HDR 12-bit against SDR 12-bit.

claim: setRecordingFormat checks `unsupportedRecordingSettings(requested)` on the current mode before the ladder rewrite at line 9768. Picking lossy DNG while the running resolution is Clear HDR is therefore refused. SPEC 2.5 says set_record_format is allowed while the ladder is active and lands on the chosen resolution's compression.
scenario: Ladder: Resolution 1 = 4K Clear HDR 16-bit none up to 25, Resolution 2 = 4K SDR 12-bit lossy_3to1 up to 50. The camera is on Resolution 1 at 24 fps, in cDNG or MLV. `set_record_format value=lossydng` is refused with "Lossy cDNG does not support Clear HDR...". Per the spec it should succeed and land on Resolution 1's compression (cDNG uncompressed). This is reachable from the WebUI Favorites Format card (see the next finding) and from core.py.
fix: Make the early check see what the ladder will run: `auto requested = settings_; requested.recordingFormat = format; ladderRewriteLocked(requested); if (const char *error = unsupportedRecordingSettings(requested)) {...}`. ladderRewriteLocked is a no-op in a take or when the ladder is inactive, so behaviour without the ladder is unchanged. The equivalent alternative is to skip the early check when ladderActiveForLocked(requested) and rely on applySettingsLocked's check of the rewritten `next`.
evidence: CameraController.cpp:9723-9729: `auto requested = settings_; requested.recordingFormat = format; if (const char *error = unsupportedRecordingSettings(requested)) { setErrorLocked(error); return false; }` runs before the ladder rewrite at 9768 (`ladderRewriteLocked(next);`). RecordingCapabilities.hpp:75-77 returns "Lossy cDNG does not support Clear HDR..." for LossyDng with clearHdr. So on a Clear HDR resolution, `set_record_format value=lossydng` is refused. SPEC 2.5 says set_record_format is "allowed; picking cDNG or lossy DNG while active lands on the chosen resolution's compression". Concrete divergence: MLV on Resolution 1 (4K Clear HDR 16-bit, none) at 24 fps. `set_record_format value=lossydng` should land on cDNG uncompressed (Resolution 1's compression) but is refused, and the camera stays in MLV. The same refusal comes from the WebUI Favorites Compression select (dispatchCdngCompressionSelection, WebControlPage.cpp:7162-7173). applySettingsLocked checks unsupportedRecordingSettings again at 10824, so moving the early check loses nothing. Low severity: the touch UI's Format list has no lossy entry, and its Compression field is locked under the ladder (ui qml/SettingsPage.qml:3223-3292).

claim: The WebUI Favorites "format" card (Resolution, Crop Mode, Compression, Bit Depth; lines 8556-8590) is not disabled while `ladder_active`. It still sends set_resolution, set_raw_bit_depth, set_cdng_compression and set_record_format+set_lossy_dng_ratio, and Core refuses those while the ladder is active. This breaks the spec rule that a UI never sends a value Core would refuse when the UI can know it in advance. The Camera settings card and the Recording format card are locked; this card is not.
scenario: Ladder active in cDNG, Format tile added to Favorites. Picking "2.39:1" or "12-bit" sends set_resolution or set_raw_bit_depth, and Core answers "The Mode Ladder picks the resolution from the FPS..." as an error toast. Picking "Lossy 3:1" sends set_record_format lossydng (ok, or refused on a Clear HDR resolution) and then set_lossy_dng_ratio, which is refused with "The Mode Ladder sets the compression...".
fix: In `case "format"`, when `snapshot.ladder_active === true`: pass disabled=true (or ladderLockedOptions) to the Resolution, Crop Mode and Bit Depth fields. Do the same for the Compression field when the format is CinemaDNG/lossy DNG. Show the same one-line note as the Recording format card ("Mode Ladder on: the FPS picks the resolution and compression.").
evidence: WebControlPage.cpp:8556-8590 (`case "format"` in the Favorites panel) was not touched by T34. The diff has no hunk between 7724 and 10241, and nothing in that range reads ladder_active. Resolution/Crop Mode (createFavoriteSelectEntryField ... `false, false` / `!cropRatioEnabled`), Bit Depth (createFavoriteSelectBlock with rawBitDepthSelectOptions, no lock) and Compression (disabled only when recording or there is no raw_compression) all stay live. They send set_resolution, set_raw_bit_depth (8586), set_record_format+set_cdng_compression and set_lossy_dng_ratio (7162-7173). Core refuses these while the ladder is active: setResolution 9242-9245, setRawBitDepth 9935-9938, setCdngCompression 9786-9789, setLossyDngRatio 9806-9809. The Recording format card applies ladderLockedOptions (11548, 11560) and the ladder note (11122-11125), so the page knows ladder_active in advance. This breaks SPEC rule 'a UI never sends something Core would refuse when the UI can know it in advance'. dispatchFavoriteCommand (8864-8870) turns each refusal into an error toast.

claim: With the probe off, the pool is empty, so the editor falls back to `rungs[].mode_ceiling` as each resolution's own-compression ceiling. Core fills `rungs[]` from runtime states in the current format (`reply.states = ladderStatesLocked(l, settings_, false)`, CameraController.cpp ladderReplyLocked). In H.264 or ProRes every rung gets the processed-video ceiling with usable=false. In MLV a lossless_jpeg rung gets MLV's ceiling. Core's validate uses own-compression states, so the editor and Core disagree.
scenario: APERTAR_SENSOR_PROBE=0 (probe off is a supported state). Camera in H.264, ladder `3840x2160:16:hdr:none:25,3840x2160:12:sdr:none`. Both rows show the same H.264 ceiling. Row 2 shows "Never used: the resolutions above already cover up to N fps." in red, and ladderDraftProblem refuses every edit, while Core's dry run reports no errors. In MLV, a lossless_jpeg row accepts "Up to" 50 (the MLV ceiling), then Core's dry run reports "above this mode's ceiling of 30 fps".
fix: Have Core put each rung's own-compression ceiling in the rung JSON. ladderReplyLocked already computes `own` (ladderStatesLocked(l, settings_, true)), so add e.g. `own_ceiling` (and own `usable`/`reason`) per rung. ladderCeiling/ladderCannotRecord use it when there is no pool entry. The simpler alternative is to treat the ceiling as unknown (ladderUnknownCeiling) whenever the rung entry's value is not in the rung's own compression, i.e. when `server.compression_applies` is false.
evidence: Core: ladderReplyLocked fills the rung JSON from runtime states, `reply.states = ladderStatesLocked(l, settings_, false)` (CameraController.cpp:9529). ModeLadder.hpp:440 writes `mode_ceiling` from those states. rungStateLocked (9409-9441) applies the rung's compression only when ownCompression or the base is cDNG/lossy DNG. In H.264, sanitizeSettingsForSensor (2871-2876) turns every rung into h264CaptureResolutionForSensor = 3840x2160, 10-bit SDR, so each rung's modeCeiling = 30 on IMX585 without the probe (tableMaximumFpsForResolution 4K SDR `sensorLimitKnown ? 60.0 : 30.0`). WebUI: with the pool empty (probe off), ladderModeInfo (5773-5778) falls back to server.rungs. ladderCeilingKnown (5813-5816) accepts it when `info.compression === rung.comp`, and ladderCeiling (5820-5827) returns `info.mode_ceiling`. The reviewer's exact ladder (`...:25,...`) does not show 'Never used', because 30 > 25. It does happen for the ladder the editor itself saves, since normalizeLadderDraft (5873-5885) clears an Up to equal to the ceiling: `3840x2160:16:hdr:none,3840x2160:12:sdr:none`. In H.264 or ProRes with the probe off, row 1 shows ceiling 30 instead of 25. Row 2 gets "Never used: the resolutions above already cover up to 30 fps." (ladderRowStates 5907-5931), and ladderDraftProblem (5888-5905) makes commitLadderDraft (6080-6090) refuse every edit. Core's own-compression validation (25, 30) reports no error. Row 1's Up to input also accepts 26-29, which Core then rejects as above the ceiling of 25.

claim: parseRungs copies the raw rung text into its error message. set_mode_ladder returns that message through errorReply, whose escapeJson (src/ipc/ControlProtocol.cpp:235) does not escape control characters below 0x20 other than \b\f\n\r\t. A rungs value that contains such a character, which the command parser accepts as a \uXXXX escape, produces an invalid JSON reply. The mode_ladder part is fine because it goes through ladder::quote.
scenario: `{"cmd":"set_mode_ladder","rungs":"3840x2160:12:sdr\u0007"}` makes the reply's "error" contain a raw 0x07 byte. Python json.load fails with "Invalid control character" (reproduced on the host with ControlProtocol.cpp and ModeLadder.hpp). Only reachable from a hand-written command, not from the UIs.
fix: In ControlProtocol.cpp escapeJson, add a default branch for bytes below 0x20 that emits \u00XX (as ladder::quote does). This fixes every errorReply. Alternatively, strip control characters from `item` before building the parseRungs error.
evidence: ControlProtocol.cpp:89-106: the command parser decodes `\u0007` into a raw 0x07 byte (appendUtf8). ModeLadder.hpp:189 builds `bad = "\"" + item + "\": expected ..."` with the raw item. setModeLadder (CameraController.cpp, its first lines) passes parseError into reply.errors and then setErrorLocked(message). ApertarCoreApp.cpp set_mode_ladder returns `errorReply(command.id, camera_.lastError(), ...)`. errorReply (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:123-134) uses escapeJson (ControlProtocol.cpp:235-252), which escapes only " \\ \b \f \n \r \t. Reproduced on the host: ModeLadder.hpp parseRungs + ControlProtocol.cpp escapeJson on rungs "3840x2160:12:sdr\x07" gives output that Python json.load rejects with 'Invalid control character at: line 1 column 40'. The mode_ladder part is valid because ladder::quote escapes control characters. Only reachable from a hand-written command, so low severity.

claim: availableFpsOptionsForSnapshot still caps the FPS pills at the current mode's IMX477 uncompressed limit while the Mode Ladder is active. The lossless caps below it are skipped when the ladder is active, but this cap is not. Core's fps_max already holds each resolution's ceiling, and Core's sanitizer applies imx477MaximumUncompressedCdngFpsForResolution per resolution. So the resolutions further down the ladder cannot be reached from the Camera settings card.
scenario: IMX477, cDNG Uncompressed, ladder [4056x3040 12-bit, 2028x1080 12-bit], running Resolution 1. Core sends fps_max 50 and ladder_tops [24, 50]. Checked in Chromium: availableFpsOptionsForSnapshot returns only ["24.000"] while maximumSupportedFpsForSnapshot returns 50. No pill selects Resolution 2, so the ladder never switches from the WebUI.
fix: Move `const ladderActive = snapshot.ladder_active === true;` above the IMX477 block and guard it with `!ladderActive &&`, as the lossless caps are. In a take, fps_take_max is already the running resolution's capped ceiling.
evidence: WebControlPage.cpp:5669-5680: the IMX477 uncompressed-cDNG block runs `max = Math.min(max, imx477MaximumUncompressedFps(width, height, …))` for the *current* snapshot resolution, with no ladder guard. Only the lossless caps below it are guarded (5682-5689 `!ladderActive && …`). Core: fillLadderFieldsLocked (CameraController.cpp:9508) sets fpsMax = ladder::ladderCeiling, which is the highest resolution's top, and each rung's ceiling already passes through the sanitizer's imx477MaximumUncompressedCdngFpsForResolution (CameraController.cpp:2910). imx477MaximumUncompressedFps gives 24 for 4056x3040 at 12-bit (5541). So when running Resolution 1 = 4056x3040 12-bit Uncompressed, max = min(fps_max, 24): every pill above 24 is filtered out (5690) and no pill reaches Resolution 2. availableFpsOptionsForSnapshot is the only source of the Camera settings card's pills (10954). In T33 the block was redundant with fps_max. In T34 it blocks the ladder.

claim: The Format card in Settings > Favorites (Resolution, Crop Mode, Compression, Bit Depth) is not disabled while ladder_active. It sends set_resolution, set_clear_hdr, set_raw_bit_depth and set_cdng_compression or set_lossy_dng_ratio, which Core refuses while the ladder is active. SPEC §1 says a UI never sends a value Core would refuse when it can know that in advance. Only the Camera settings card and the Recording format card were locked.
scenario: Mock with ladder_active true and ui.favorites_order ["format"]. The favorites card shows the Resolution select (clearhdr) and the 16-bit and 12-bit pills enabled. Clicking 12-bit sends {"cmd":"set_raw_bit_depth","value":12} and shows the error toast 'The Mode Ladder picks the resolution from the FPS. Turn it off…'. The Compression select first sends set_record_format (accepted) and then set_cdng_compression (refused).
fix: In the favorites `case "format"` block, take `const ladderActive = snapshot.ladder_active === true;`. Pass it as the disabled flag of both Resolution fields and the Crop Mode field (OR it with !cropRatioEnabled). Add it to the Compression field's disabled expression (the field is shown only in CinemaDNG). Map rawBitDepthSelectOptions with `enabled: … && !ladderActive` for the Bit Depth block, or use ladderLockedOptions. Optionally add the same one-line note as the Recording format card.
evidence: renderFavoriteControls `case "format"` (WebControlPage.cpp:8556-8589) has no ladder check anywhere: the Resolution/Crop entry fields pass disabled=false or !cropRatioEnabled (8559-8566), the plain Resolution field passes false (8568-8570), and Compression is disabled only for recording or no raw_compression (8582-8585). Bit Depth uses rawBitDepthOptionEnabled (8325-8329, 7233-7247), which ignores ladder_active. By contrast, the Recording format card uses `&& !ladderActive` (11584) and ladderLockedOptions (11560). Core refuses these commands while active: setResolution (CameraController.cpp:9242-9244), setRawBitDepth (9935-9937) and setClearHdr (9975-9977) return kLadderPicksMode; setCdngCompression and setLossyDngRatio (9786-9788, 9806-9808) return kLadderSetsCompression. dispatchCdngCompressionSelection (7163-7174) sends set_record_format (accepted) and then set_cdng_compression or set_lossy_dng_ratio (refused). The UI knows ladder_active in advance, so this breaks SPEC §0's 'No illegal values' rule. 'format' is a selectable favorite (4752).

claim: In the pointer drag, `over` defaults to the last row whenever the pointer is not inside a .ladder-row box. The transition lines and the 10 px gaps between rows therefore map to the last position. On a phone the transition text wraps to 3-4 lines, so a large part of the space between rows is affected.
scenario: 3 resolutions. Drag row 3's handle up and release over the 'Above 25 fps: …' line between rows 1 and 2: no row is marked as the drop target and nothing moves. Drag row 1's handle and release over the line between rows 2 and 3: row 3 (the last) is marked and the move goes to the end, then is refused as 'would never be used' (both checked in Chromium).
fix: Pick the slot by row midpoints: `let over = all.length - 1; for (let i = 0; i < all.length; i++) { const b = all[i].getBoundingClientRect(); if (event.clientY < b.top + b.height / 2) { over = i; break; } }`, so gaps and transition lines map to the nearest slot.
evidence: installLadderDrag pointermove (WebControlPage.cpp:6140-6151) starts with `let over = event.clientY < all[0].getBoundingClientRect().top ? 0 : all.length - 1;` and changes it only when clientY falls inside a `.ladder-row` box. rows() selects `#settingsModeLadderList .ladder-row` (6122). The transition line is a sibling `.ladder-transition` inside `.ladder-item`, outside `.ladder-row` (6197-6200, 6203). The list has a 10px gap and each item an 8px gap (CSS 2093-2107). So any pointer over a transition line or a gap between rows 1 and 2 sets over = last. Dragging row 3 there gives over === from (no highlight, no move). Dragging row 1 between rows 2 and 3 targets the end (6129-6130 → moveLadderRung(0, last)), and that move can then be refused by ladderDraftProblem. The fallback is clearly meant only for 'below the list'.

claim: ladderDraftFromServer keeps a saved 'Up to' that equals the mode's ceiling (for example 25 on 4K Clear HDR 16-bit, as core.py or an older save can write it). normalizeLadderDraft clears it to '' on the first edit. Because ladderDirty compares rung text, the draft stays 'Unsaved changes' with Save enabled even after the user undoes the edit. Saving also silently drops the saved threshold.
scenario: Saved rungs_text '3840x2160:16:hdr:none:25,3840x2160:12:sdr:none'. Type 40 in Resolution 2, then clear it again. Result: 'Unsaved changes…', Save enabled, and Resolution 1's Up to changes from '25' to '' (checked in Chromium). Save sends '3840x2160:16:hdr:none,…'.
fix: Normalize the draft on load (`state.ladderDraft = normalizeLadderDraft(ladderDraftFromServer(modeLadder))` in applyModeLadder and revertModeLadder). Compute ladderDirty against `ladderDraftText(normalizeLadderDraft(ladderDraftFromServer(state.ladderServer)))`, not the raw rungs_text.
evidence: ladderDraftFromServer (WebControlPage.cpp:5839-5848) keeps any threshold > 0 as thr text. Core stores and echoes a threshold equal to the ceiling: validate errors only on `threshold > modeCeiling + eps` (ModeLadder.hpp:286), and rungsText writes it (245). Besides core.py, this happens when a build-max change lowers the ceiling to an existing threshold, or after a save made while the ceiling was unknown (ladderUnknownCeiling 280, 5740/5823). commitLadderDraft (6080-6090) runs normalizeLadderDraft over the whole list. Its `value < ceiling` test (5880) clears another resolution's '25' when the ceiling is 25. ladderDirty (5855-5857) compares raw draft text with server rungs_text. So after editing Resolution 2 and undoing it, the draft text is '3840x2160:16:hdr:none,…' while rungs_text is '…:none:25,…': it stays dirty with Save enabled, and Resolution 1's field changed although the user never touched it.

claim: state.fpsSwitchingTo is one global value. Each set_fps click's finally block clears it without checking that it still holds that click's target. When two resolution-changing FPS picks overlap, the first reply removes 'Switching to Resolution N…' while the second switch is still in flight. The topline then shows the first reply's stale ladder_text.
scenario: Ladder [25, 40, 50]. Click 30 (switch to Resolution 2), then 45 (switch to Resolution 3) 150 ms later. In the mock, once the first reply arrives the line reads 'Resolution 2 · 3840×2160 · SDR12 · ≤40 · Uncompressed' while Core is moving to Resolution 3. With Core's mutex this also holds on the camera.
fix: Keep the target in a local variable and clear only your own: `const switching = target !== ladderRung ? target : 0; state.fpsSwitchingTo = switching; … finally { if (switching && state.fpsSwitchingTo === switching) { state.fpsSwitchingTo = 0; if (state.snapshot) renderSnapshot(state.snapshot); } }`.
evidence: FPS pill handler (WebControlPage.cpp:11477-11497): `state.fpsSwitchingTo = target !== ladderRung ? target : 0;`, then in finally `if (state.fpsSwitchingTo) { state.fpsSwitchingTo = 0; renderSnapshot(...) }`, with no check that the value is still this click's target. sendCommand does not serialize requests (10698-10733): concurrent fetches. Its optimistic set_fps patch (10285-10287) re-renders, so the second click's closure sees ladderRung = state.fpsSwitchingTo (11475). The second click sets fpsSwitchingTo = 3. When the first reply arrives, its finally clears it. The line at 11505-11507 then shows snapshot.ladder_text (Resolution 2) while the second set_fps, which changes the resolution, is still in flight. That breaks SPEC §3: 'while a set_fps that changes the resolution is in flight: Switching to Resolution N…'.

claim: With the sensor probe off, Core sends sensor_area {0,0} and crop null for every resolution. ladderCrop then uses the mode's own size as the sensor area, so every resolution is drawn as a full window and described as 'Whole sensor area, no crop.' That is a made-up claim; SPEC §1.6 says crop diagrams come from the probe, not guesses.
scenario: APERTAR_SENSOR_PROBE=0 and a saved resolution 2560x1440:12:sdr (a real crop-in) or 3840x1608 (letterboxed). The row and the Running now graphic both say 'Whole sensor area, no crop.' with a full green window.
fix: In ladderCrop, set `const areaKnown = Number(sensorArea.width) > 0;`. When !areaKnown && !known, return desc '' (or 'Crop unknown: sensor probe off.'), a title without 'Full sensor area', and cropIn false. Keep the SPEC fallback drawing but use the plain-window fill, not the 'whole' style.
evidence: With the probe off, probedSensorArea() has no crops (CameraController.cpp:3047-3057), so sensor_area is {0,0}. Each rung's crop is serialised as null (ModeLadder.hpp:403-406, 442). The probe defaults on but is switchable (APERTAR_SENSOR_PROBE, CameraController.cpp:6255), and the WebUI handles this case on purpose (6390 'Sensor probe off…'). In ladderCrop (WebControlPage.cpp:5934-5960), area falls back to mode.width*binning × mode.height*binning (5939-5941), and width/height = min(area, size) gives the same values. So `whole` is true (5948), and desc becomes 'Whole sensor area, no crop.' (or 'Whole sensor area, binned 2×2…') for every mode (5954-5956), with title 'Full sensor area …'. That includes table modes such as IMX585 3840x1608 (rows not read) or a crop-in. Both callers show it: the row (6171, 6216) and the Running now graphic (6487). SPEC §3 allows a fallback drawing, but this text states an untrue fact about the readout, and §1.6 says crop facts come from the probe, not guesses.

claim: In availableFpsOptionsForSnapshot the IMX477 uncompressed-cDNG cap is still applied for the current mode while the Mode Ladder is active. T34 gated only the lossless caps with !ladderActive (line 5682). Core's fps_max already holds each resolution's own uncompressed cap, because rungStateLocked runs the sanitiser with the rung's compression (CameraController.cpp:2905-2911). So the extra cap for the running mode hides every FPS that would switch to a faster resolution. The touch UI gates this cap correctly (CameraPage.qml:828-833).
scenario: Checked in Chromium against the mock (page functions called directly). IMX477, cDNG uncompressed, ladder active with ladder_tops [30,100] and fps_max 100. Running 4056x2160 12-bit, the Camera settings FPS pills are only 24/25/30. Running 4056x3040, only 24. The 50/60/100 pills that would move to Resolution 2 (2028x1080) never appear, so the ladder cannot switch resolution from the WebUI FPS pills. The same snapshot gives 24…100 when the running mode is 2028x1080.
fix: In availableFpsOptionsForSnapshot, move `const ladderActive = snapshot.ladder_active === true;` above the IMX477 block and make its condition `!ladderActive && !stillCaptureForSnapshot(snapshot) && sensorLower.indexOf("imx477") !== -1 && ...`, as CameraPage.qml:828 does. In a take this changes nothing: fps_take_max is the running rung's own ceiling, which already holds the cap.
evidence: WebControlPage.cpp:5668-5679: the IMX477 uncompressed-cDNG block (`max = Math.min(max, imx477MaximumUncompressedFps(width, height, raw_bit_depth))`) has no ladder guard. `ladderActive` is declared only at 5683, and only the three lossless caps (5684-5689) check it. While the ladder is active, Core sends fps_max = ladder::ladderCeiling, the highest rungCeiling (CameraController.cpp:9506-9508, ModeLadder.hpp:137-143). Each rung's ceiling comes from sanitizeSettingsForSensor run with that rung's compression (rungStateLocked 9425-9431). The sanitiser already applies the IMX477 uncompressed cap per mode (CameraController.cpp:2905-2911). maximumSupportedFpsForSnapshot returns fps_max (5593-5596), and the old per-mode table then cuts it again. imx477MaximumUncompressedFps(4056,2160,12) = 30 and (4056,3040,12) = 24 (5541-5545). With fps_max 100 the result is max = 30 (or 24). The presets filter at 5690 then drops 50/60/100, so the pills that would move to Resolution 2 (built at 11475-11500 from the same fpsOptions, call at 10954) never appear. The touch UI wraps the same cap in `if (!root.ladderActive)` (CameraPage.qml:828-833).

claim: formatDisplaySubtext now carries Core's whole running line. It is shown in InfoLine's sub Text (InfoLine.qml:64-72), which has a fixed width and no elide, wrap or clip. The line is about 2.5 times wider than its column, so it draws across the preview and the centred bottom controls.
scenario: Default 720x720 square layout: bottomStatsWidth 180 minus icon 18 and spacing 8 leaves a 154 px text column. Measured with Inter Regular at 13 px, 'Resolution 1 · 3840×2160 · ClearHDR16 · ≤25 · Uncompressed' is 379 px wide and 'Mode Ladder on · the next FPS pick chooses the resolution' is 362 px. The FORMAT sub line, at y≈610-625, runs from x≈46 to x≈425. That is across the clip-browser button and centre stack of bottomControlsRow, which is centred at x=360 and covers y≈606-680. Compact landscape is the same: 263 px of text in a 120 px column.
fix: InfoLine.qml: give the sub Text `wrapMode: Text.WordWrap`, `maximumLineCount: 3`, `elide: Text.ElideRight`. Give the inner Column an id and set `height: Math.max(sub.length > 0 ? heightWithSub : heightWithoutSub, <column>.implicitHeight)`, so the stats column grows upward (it is bottom-anchored). The other InfoLines keep their size because their subs fit on one line.
evidence: CameraPage.qml:526-527: formatDisplaySubtext is controlBridge.ladderText whenever it is non-empty. It is passed as `sub` to the FORMAT InfoLine (CameraPage.qml:3646-3660), whose width is bottomStatsWidth: 180 in the default square layout and 136 in compact landscape (line 182). In InfoLine.qml:64-72 the sub Text has `width: parent.width` and no wrapMode, elide or clip. InfoLine's height is fixed (heightWithSub, line 21), so a single-line Text draws past its width. Measured with the shipped qml/fonts/Inter/Inter-Regular.ttf: at 13 px, 'Resolution 1 · 3840×2160 · ClearHDR16 · ≤25 · Uncompressed' is 379 px and 'Mode Ladder on · the next FPS pick chooses the resolution' is 362 px, against a 154 px column (180-18-8). At 9 px (compact landscape) the first is 263 px against a 120 px column (136-11-5). The text starts at x≈46 and reaches about x≈425. That is past the horizontal centre, into bottomControlsRow, which is centred (line 3742) on the same bottom band. Before T34 the sub line was at most about 93 px ('Uncompressed'). The design's short prefix ('HDR16 · ≤25 · Uncompressed') would have fit. The SPEC's full running line does not.

claim: applyLadderToPreset builds the Favorite's mode as `named = sanitize(preset)`. But Favorites carry no Clear HDR field. apply_preset starts from camera_.settings() (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:11178ff), so `preset.clearHdr` is the camera's current flag, not the Favorite's. When the Favorite's FPS falls on a resolution on the other side of Clear HDR/SDR, `named` becomes a mode the Favorite never had. The load is refused, and the message names that mode.
scenario: Patrik's ladder is on Resolution 1 (4K Clear HDR 16-bit, 24 fps). He loads a Favorite saved before the ladder in 4K SDR 12-bit uncompressed at 50 fps. presetSettings has clearHdr=true (inherited from the camera) and bits 12, so named = 4K Clear HDR 12-bit. The ladder runs 50 fps in 4K SDR 12-bit, the modes differ, and the load is refused: "This Favorite records 4K Clear HDR 12-bit at 50 fps; the Mode Ladder runs 50 fps in 4K SDR 12-bit. ..." But that Favorite is exactly Resolution 2. The reverse also fails: on Resolution 2, a 16-bit 24 fps Favorite sanitises to 4K SDR 12-bit (SDR has no 16-bit) and is refused, although Resolution 1 is that mode. 'Save the Favorite again' cannot fix it, because Clear HDR is never stored. With the ladder on, no Favorite can move the camera across the Clear HDR boundary (WebUI and touch UI alike).
fix: In applyLadderToPreset, build `named` with the Clear HDR the ladder chose, except where the Favorite's bit depth implies Clear HDR: `CaptureSettings asNamed = preset; asNamed.clearHdr = chosen.clearHdr || (sensorFamily == SensorFamily::Imx585 && preset.rawBitDepth == 16); const ladder::Rung named = ladderRungOf(sanitizeSettingsForSensor(asNamed, sensorFamily));`. Build the refusal text from this `named`.
evidence: ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10928 `CaptureSettings presetSettings = camera_.settings();`. No apply_preset field sets clearHdr: the handler at 10888-11185 has no Clear HDR key, and Favorites never store one (bridge cameraPresetSettings, ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1152-1184; WebUI allowedKeys, WebControlPage.cpp:12200-12241). So `preset.clearHdr` is the camera's current flag. CameraController.cpp:10742 `named = ladderRungOf(sanitizeSettingsForSensor(preset, ...))`, and ModeLadder.hpp:88-91 sameMode compares clearHdr and bits. supportedRawBitDepthForSensor (CC:2846-2850) turns Clear HDR 12/16 into 12 or 16 and SDR 16 into 12. First case, on R1 (Clear HDR 16): a 12-bit 50 fps SDR Favorite gives named = Clear HDR 12-bit. ladderRewriteLocked (CC:9466-9488) picks R2 = SDR 12. The modes differ, so the load is refused at CC:10744. Reverse case, on R2 (SDR): a 16-bit 24 fps Favorite sanitises to SDR 12-bit, the ladder picks R1 (Clear HDR 16-bit), and the load is refused, although that Favorite is R1. Whether the load works depends on which resolution the camera is on, not on the Favorite. Saving the Favorite again cannot fix it, because Clear HDR is never stored.

claim: availablePcfFpsOptions caps the PCF pot and fps_up/fps_down list at settings.fpsMax. With the ladder active, T34 sets fpsMax to the ladder ceiling (CameraController.cpp:9508) even during a take. A take is capped at fps_take_max, the running resolution's ceiling. So in a take the hardware list offers FPS values Core will silently not reach. The WebUI and touch UI switch to fps_take_max when recording; the PCF does not.
scenario: Speed ramping is allowed. A take starts at 24 on Resolution 1 (fps_take_max 25, fps_max 50). The PCF list is [24, 25, 30, 50]. Turning the pot into its upper half, or pressing fps_up at 25, sends set_fps 30/50. Core caps it to 25 and replies ok, so nothing changes and no message appears. The pot sits at '50' while the camera runs 25, and every analog event in that range re-sends set_fps and emits a settings event. In T33 this take's list stopped at 25.
fix: Give availablePcfFpsOptions a `bool recording` parameter and use `const double coreMax = recording && settings.fpsTakeMax > 0.0 ? settings.fpsTakeMax : settings.fpsMax;` in place of settings.fpsMax. Pass camera_.isRecording() (or the recording state the App already holds) from App:8758 and App:9023.
evidence: CameraController.cpp:9497-9521 fillLadderFieldsLocked sets `out.fpsMax = ladder::ladderCeiling(...)` whenever the ladder is active, with no recording check. fpsTakeMax becomes the running resolution's top. settings() (CC:10614-10622) fills these fields. ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1208 `maxFps = settings.fpsMax > 0.0 ? settings.fpsMax : ...` has no take branch. Its callers are the analog pot (App:8758) and fps_up/fps_down/cycle (App:9023-9028). In a take, setFps (CC:9302-9316) caps to `ladderFields.fpsTakeMax`; when that equals the current fps it returns true silently (`!ladderMoves && |settings_.fps - effectiveFps| < 0.0001` → emitSettingsEventLocked, ok). Example on R1 (top 25, ladder ceiling 50): the take list is [24,25,30,50]. A cycle press at 25 picks index 2 (30) via nextPcfPresetIndex (App:1113-1114). Core caps it to 25, so every later press picks 30 again and the cycle never returns to 24. The pot's upper half is dead, with no message. In T33 fpsMax was the mode ceiling, so this take's list was [24,25].

claim: The WebUI Favorites 'Format' card (renderFavoriteControls, case "format", lines 8556-8589) was not made ladder-aware. Its Resolution, Crop Mode, Compression and Bit Depth controls stay live while ladder_active. They send set_resolution, set_clear_hdr, set_raw_bit_depth, set_cdng_compression and set_lossy_dng_ratio, which Core refuses with the ladder on. This breaks SPEC §0: a UI never sends what it knows Core would refuse.
scenario: The ladder is active and Patrik uses the Format card in his Favorites tab. Picking 'Full HD' in Resolution, or a crop, gives the toast "The Mode Ladder picks the resolution from the FPS...". Picking 12-bit in Bit Depth on Resolution 1 is refused the same way. Picking 'Lossy 3:1' in Compression on Resolution 2 sends set_record_format lossydng, which the ladder silently rewrites back to uncompressed cDNG; then set_lossy_dng_ratio is refused with "The Mode Ladder sets the compression...". The Recording format card locks these controls; this card does not.
fix: In case "format", read `const ladderActive = snapshot.ladder_active === true;`. Disable Resolution with `ladderActive`, Crop Mode with `!cropRatioEnabled || ladderActive`, and Compression with `... || ladderActive`; the plain Resolution select in the non-crop branch also gets `ladderActive`. Map the Bit Depth options through ladderLockedOptions(rawBitDepthSelectOptions, ladderActive), or return early in its handler. Add the line 'Mode Ladder on: the FPS picks the resolution and compression.' when ladderActive.
evidence: WebControlPage.cpp:8556-8589 (renderFavoriteControls, case "format") never reads snapshot.ladder_active. The only uses are 5683, 6013, 6466, 10245 and 10955-11584, i.e. the Recording format card and the Camera settings card. Its Resolution select (8559-8562) sends resolutionBaseCommands → set_resolution. Crop Mode (8563-8565) is disabled only by `!cropRatioEnabled`. Compression (8578-8582) is disabled only while recording or without raw_compression, and goes through dispatchCdngCompressionSelection (7163-7174) → set_record_format + set_cdng_compression or set_lossy_dng_ratio. Bit Depth (8584-8588) sends set_raw_bit_depth. Core refuses these while the ladder is active: kLadderPicksMode at CC:9243/9936/9976, kLadderSetsCompression at CC:9787/9807. dispatchFavoriteCommand (8864-8870) then shows the refusal as a toast. The UI knows ladder_active, so this breaks SPEC §0 ('a UI never sends something Core would refuse when the UI can know it in advance'), and the §3 locking applied to the Recording format card is missing here.

claim: The touch Settings 'Mode Ladder' toggle ignores the result of applyModeLadderEnabled. When Core refuses to turn the ladder on, the switch stays off with no message, although the bridge holds Core's error in lastError.
scenario: Patrik lowers max_fps to 24 in the Config panel; Resolution 2 now 'would never be used'. (Or: a ladder saved with core.py as `...:12:sdr:none:50`, with max_fps then set to 30.) He turns the ladder off on the touch screen, which is always allowed. Later he turns it on: Core refuses with the joined validation errors, the pill springs back to off, and nothing says why. The WebUI shows the same refusal as a toast.
fix: `onToggled: function(value) { if (!apertarControlBridge.applyModeLadderEnabled(value)) modeLadderRow.errorText = apertarControlBridge.lastError }`, shown as a red line under the caption and cleared on the next success or on ladderChanged. Or use the page's existing warning popup.
evidence: qml/SettingsPage.qml:3332-3340: the pill is enabled when not recording and ladderCount > 0, and `onToggled: function(value) { apertarControlBridge.applyModeLadderEnabled(value) }` ignores the bool result. The bridge (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:300-306) only returns sendCoreCommand's result. The error lands in lastError, but no QML shows apertarControlBridge.lastError for this, and there is no global lastErrorChanged handler (grep of qml/). TogglePill.qml:59-63 only emits toggled, and `checked` stays bound to ladderEnabled, so the pill stays off. Core does refuse turning the ladder on: CC setModeLadder `if (!reply.errors.empty() && (rungs || draft.enabled))` refuses with the joined validation errors. Saved ladders can become invalid later: with max_fps=24 in apertar-hardware.conf, a Clear HDR 16 + SDR 12 ladder gets 'Resolution 2 would never be used...' (ModeLadder.hpp:292-295), and setBuildMaximumFps (CC) does not change the saved ladder. Result: Patrik taps an enabled switch and nothing happens, with no reason, although Core sent one.
